text:
maria: Heads-up — starting a short planning thread for route identity coalescence + the spline backfill. Goal: collapse legacy route_id variants into canonical_route_id without breaking console queries or quota billing.

jordan: quick q — are we doing dual-write for telemetry while backfilling?

maria: yes dual-write for 4 weeks, read-gating by header if present. primary write stays unchanged until canary is green.

oliver: +1 on dual-write. can we do a gradual keyspace split so console dashboards don't spike p99 on joins?

maria: plan is: 1) new canonical field route_identity.v2, 2) consumer-side read adapter that prefers v2 when present, 3) backfill job (spline) to populate v2 for history, 4) rollout routing rule in ingest to emit both keys.

kevin: does the backfill maintain route->tenant mapping immutability? I worry about alias churn causing mismatch for quotas.

sasha: we should preserve alias history in a small lookup table used by billing to ensure quota attribution stays stable during transition.

jordan: any perf estimates for spline backfill? rough token: 10B rows across shards.

oliver: from a probe run on a single shard: ~1.2M rows/hr with current worker config. can parallelize by tenant-group, but need to watch DB throttles.

maria: initial run will run at 20% throughput to avoid impact. we also plan to emit backfill-progress metric to console.

kevin: billing: if canonical id isn't present we fallback to legacy id. Can we add an audit flag to mark records that switched mapping?

maria: yes, backfill writes a _migration_meta field with {"spline_v": "1", "applied_at": "<ts>"} so downstream can detect.

jordan: will console query paths need updates? e.g., /v1/routes/stats currently queries route_id = X.

oliver: minimal changes: the read adapter will rewrite queries to OR on canonical_route_id OR legacy_ids for a grace period, then toggle to prefer canonical.

sasha: telemetry team: we need to ensure the console dashboards' materialized views include canonical id post-cutover. Sort of a safe-read gating plan please.

maria: action item: oliver to add read-adapter + query rewrite PR, sasha to coordinate dashboard MV changes, kevin to draft billing alias table schema, jordan to create backfill runbook with throttling knobs.

oliver: I'll open PR tonight. sample adapter snippet: `if (req.header.x-route-canary == 'v2') { use canonical } else { try canonical fallback legacy }`

kevin: billing alias table sketch: `route_alias(route_id, canonical_route_id, valid_from, valid_to, source)` — will add retention note.

ingest-bot: deploy-notice: ingest-api will support dual-write flag in next canary deploy (build 8f3a2e) — scheduled 21:00 UTC.

jordan: thanks. also, let's add a sentinel metric `spline.backfill.delay` to catch slowdowns.

maria: agreed. final note: we'll run a small canary on 5 prod tenants next week, monitor console p95/p99, billing delta, and query errors. If all green, widen to 50% then full.

sasha: thanks everyone — I'll sync with dashboard owners and post the MV migration checklist in this thread when ready.

kevin: adding a TODO to include rollback steps if alias mapping mismatch >0.1% of traffic.

maria: perfect. closing the planning thread for now — will update with links to PRs and the backfill runbook. :thumbsup:
